$comment: THE RULES ARE DATA, AND THEY ARE MEANT TO BE SWAPPED. Replace this file and the checker changes. Nothing here is copied from a standard that restricts who may use it: the wording is our own, and a licensed word list can be dropped in as a rules file of its own.

$omitted.just: CONSIDERED AND LEFT OUT, and written into voice.md instead. It has two meanings, the minimiser and the time word, and a word-boundary pattern cannot tell them apart. MEASURED: adding it refuses 5 lines in this project's own documents, and 4 of them are the time word: 'somebody who has just arrived' twice, 'the thing that just happened', 'a settings file that just changed'. One is the minimiser: 'a newly reachable tree is just more filesystem'. A rule that is wrong four times out of five is a rule a writer turns off. So the rule lives in doc/guidance/voice.md, where a person applies it, and not here.

rules.name: no semicolon
rules.says: a semicolon joins two sentences that should be two

rules.name: do not tell the reader how to feel
rules.says: the word tells the reader how to feel about the sentence, and this file is the whole list
